Trump annonce « réduire considérablement » des exercices militaires avec la Corée du Sud Getty Images via AFP. D onald Trump a annoncé « réduire considérablement » la participation des Etats-Unis aux exercices militaires annuels avec la Corée du Sud qui ont débuté lundi, invoquant en particulier sa « très bonne relation avec Kim Jong Un », le dirigeant nord-coréen. L’édition de cette année, prévue sur onze jours, doit notamment prendre en compte l’expérience acquise par les troupes nord-coréennes aux côtés de l’armée russe sur le front ukrainien. L’annonce de M. Trump, réalisée sur sa plateforme Truth Social, vient s’inscrire dans la longue liste de camouflets adressés par le président américain à des alliés historiques des Etats-Unis depuis son retour à la Maison-Blanche en 2025. Donald Trump dénonce dans son message des exercices « coûteux » et qui selon lui « envoient un signal totalement inapproprié et hostile » envers la Corée du Nord. Un pays qui, « depuis que Donald Trump est président, s’est montré non menaçant et respectueux », a-t-il ajouté à la troisième personne. Baptisés « Ulchi Freedom Shield », ces exercices annuels devaient initialement mobiliser 18.000 soldats sud-coréens ainsi que des effectifs issus du contingent américain de 28.500 hommes stationnés dans le pays. Le ministère de la Défense sud-coréen a affirmé lundi que ces manœuvres avaient commencé « comme prévu ». Aguerrissement Rendez-vous estival régulier pour les forces armées sud-coréennes et leurs alliés américains, ces exercices sont conçus pour renforcer la défense contre la Corée du Nord, pays doté de l’arme nucléaire et qui multiplie les essais de missiles. Les manœuvres devaient être placées cette année sous le signe de l’aguerrissement dont les effectifs de Pyongyang ont bénéficié sur le front ukrainien, dans le cadre d’un rapprochement stratégique avec Moscou. « Ils en ont tiré des enseignements et les ont rapportés en Corée du Nord », avait souligné le 10 août le colonel Ryan Donald, porte-parole du Commandement combiné des forces américaines et sud-coréennes. « Cela modifie les capacités de la RPDC, et notre entraînement prend en compte cette menace », notamment en matière d’usage de drones, de cyberattaques et de brouillage GPS, avait ajouté l’officier, en utilisant l’acronyme désignant la République populaire démocratique de Corée. Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a récemment accusé Pyongyang de se préparer à envoyer entre 30.000 et 50.000 soldats supplémentaires pour appuyer les forces russes, sans préciser l’origine de ces chiffres ni de potentiel calendrier. Dimanche, les médias d’Etat nord-coréens ont souligné que Kim Jong Un s’était dit « fier » de sa relation avec la Russie, dans une lettre envoyée au président Vladimir Poutine. « Non merci ! » Sur Truth Social, Donald Trump a également fait mention de la non-participation de Séoul aux opérations militaires américaines contre l’Iran pour justifier une réduction de voilure américaine. Le président sud-coréen Lee Jae Myung avait affirmé en juin, en pleine accalmie dans le conflit entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran, que Donald Trump souhaitait à présent se concentrer sur la résolution de « la question nord-coréenne ». Considéré comme conciliant envers la Corée du Nord, Lee Jae Myung a pris le contrepied de son prédécesseur, réputé pour sa fermeté, depuis son arrivée au pouvoir en juin 2025, offrant à Pyongyang des pourparlers sans conditions préalables. Mais les autorités de Corée du Nord n’ont pour l’instant pas donné suite à ces offres répétées. « Kim Jong Un et moi » La veille de son annonce, Donald Trump avait publié sur Truth Social une image le montrant aux côtés de Kim Jong Un lors de leur rencontre historique en 2019, pendant le premier mandat du milliardaire. « Malgré les apparences peu amicales sur cette photo en particulier, il y en a beaucoup où nous sourions », avait-il écrit comme légende, ajoutant : « Kim Jong Un et moi, nous nous entendons TRES BIEN ! » Pyongyang avait dénoncé jeudi les exercices militaires conjoints à venir entre Washington et Séoul, et prévenu d’une possible riposte par des mesures « de dissuasion » renforcées. La Corée du Nord voit dans ces exercices une répétition en vue d’une invasion et a tiré mercredi un missile balistique au-dessus de la mer du Japon en signe de protestation. « Notre principe constant, pour garantir la sécurité, est de répondre à un nouveau niveau de menace par un nouveau niveau de dissuasion », avait déclaré jeudi un porte-parole du ministère nord-coréen des Affaires étrangères. Pour Leif-Eric Easley, professeur d’études internationales à l’université Ewha de Séoul, une réduction des manœuvres conjointes « affaiblira la dissuasion face à d’éventuels conflits en Asie ». « Les économies réalisées » le cas échéant « sont marginales, tandis que les avantages diplomatiques pour les relations avec la Corée du Nord sont incertains », relève-t-il pour l’AFP. Donald Trump annonce une réduction majeure des exercices militaires américains en Corée du Sud, invoquant ses relations avec Kim Jong Un et la volonté d’apaiser les tensions avec Pyongyang. Les exportations stimulent les bénéfices du constructeur automobile chinois Geely En avril, mai et juin, le chiffre d'affaires s'est élevé à 89,8 milliards de yuans (11,5 milliards d'euros), soit une hausse de 15%. Le bénéfice a progressé de 36% pour atteindre 4,9 milliards de yuans (627 millions d'euros), conformément aux prévisions des analystes. Au cours du premier semestre, le bénéfice a toutefois légèrement reculé, de 1,8%, pour s'établir à 9,09 milliards de yuans. Au cours des six premiers mois de 2026, Geely a plus que doublé ses exportations, écoulant 474.228 véhicules à l'étranger. Le constructeur a ainsi pu compenser en partie la baisse de la demande sur son marché intérieur : en Chine, les ventes totales d'automobiles ont chuté d'un cinquième et la fédération du secteur prévoit une baisse de 14% pour l'ensemble de l'année 2026. Les chiffres d'exportation de Geely sont toutefois inférieurs à ceux de son concurrent chinois BYD, le plus grand constructeur mondial de véhicules électriques. Ce dernier a exporté 812.700 voitures au cours du premier semestre. Geely travaille à la mise en place de capacités de production supplémentaires hors de Chine. Le mois dernier, il a été annoncé que le groupe avait conclu un accord pour construire des voitures dans l'usine de la marque américaine Ford à Valence, en Espagne. Et grâce à une coentreprise avec le constructeur français Renault, une production locale va également voir le jour au Brésil. Geely Automobile fait partie de Geely Holding. Ce groupe privé chinois détient notamment Volvo Cars, Polestar et Lotus. Le constructeur automobile chinois Geely Automobile - qui possède des marques telles que Geely, Zeekr et Lynk & Co - a réussi à augmenter ses bénéfices de plus d'un tiers au second semestre. Le fort niveau d'exportation a compensé le recul de la demande intérieure. Mis à jour le 17/08/2026 à 08:25

Incendie dans les Fagnes : le Roi se rendra en matinée à la rencontre des équipes qui luttent contre le feu AFP. L e roi Philippe se rendra lundi en fin de matinée au centre de crise provincial de Vottem et aux abords des Fagnes pour rencontrer les équipes mobilisées pour lutter contre l’incendie qui frappe la région depuis vendredi, a annoncé lundi le Palais royal dans un communiqué. Le Roi sera d’abord informé de l’évolution de la situation et des opérations en cours à Vottem, avant de se rendre au centre de coordination établi aux abords des incendies. Il ira ainsi « témoigner son soutien aux personnes engagées sur le terrain et prendre la mesure de l’ampleur des dégâts », précise le Palais royal. Samedi, le roi Philippe avait déjà exprimé, dans un bref communiqué, « sa gratitude aux services de secours ainsi qu’à toutes les personnes mobilisées pour lutter contre l’incendie, parmi lesquelles la Défense, les agriculteurs de la région et les pompiers allemands venus en renfort ». Un important incendie frappe la région des Fagnes depuis vendredi après-midi. Près de 3.000 hectares sont partis en fumée, selon le dernier bilan provisoire communiqué dimanche soir par les autorités. Iran province suspends plan for sharply higher petrol price. A plan to sell petrol at a much higher “refinery cost” rate in southern Kerman province was halted hours before it was due to begin, the provincial fuel distribution company said on Thursday.

Land routes cannot replace Iran’s blocked sea trade, chamber official warns. Replacing a single ship carrying essential goods to Iran would require about 2,500 trucks, a Chamber of Commerce official warned, saying land routes cannot offset the US maritime blockade and negotiations are the only realistic way to restore trade.

Caspian Sea hits 200-year low as Iran debates the treaty meant to divide it. The Caspian Sea is falling by as much as 20 centimeters a year and stands at its lowest level in two centuries, an Iranian environment official said, a warning that lands just as Tehran reopens the argument over how to divide a sea that is shrinking on all five of its owners.

Iranian forces used cultural sites, medical clinics in Alborz crackdown. Security forces used cultural venues and medical clinics as firing positions, ammunition stores and sites for holding bodies during Iran's January 2026 protest crackdown in Alborz province, according to material reviewed by Iran International.

How Iran’s Supreme National Security Council works, and who gets a vote. Iran’s Supreme National Security Council brings together the country’s most powerful officials, but its workings are less straightforward than its name suggests, as even its secretary, often dubbed Iran’s security chief, does not automatically have a vote.

Tehran’s reshuffle leaves no pragmatic opening. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei’s latest appointments to Iran’s top security and paramilitary institutions are not routine personnel changes but a reflection of his priorities for tighter control over the institutions directing war and domestic repression.

US vows 'indefinite' blockade as Iran signals offensive posture. The US-Iran standoff is hardening around the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington saying it can sustain maritime pressure indefinitely and Tehran signaling readiness for a prolonged confrontation and more offensive operations.

Iran lawmakers push back on regional monitoring of Hormuz. A dispute in Iran’s parliament over the terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz is threatening to complicate negotiations in Muscat, as lawmakers challenge a proposed role for Oman and Pakistan in monitoring shipping through the waterway.

Iran crackdown grinds on with new wave of prison terms. Iranian courts have handed down a new wave of prison terms and other punishments against protesters, activists and citizens accused of national security offenses, as the judicial crackdown that followed January’s nationwide protests continues months later.

'Better than nukes'? Iran digs in on Hormuz as US deal nears end. Iran is doubling down on control of the Strait of Hormuz, with some in Tehran now arguing the strategic leverage it provides is more valuable than a nuclear weapon.

Democrats turn Iran war costs against Trump as midterms near. US Democrats appear to be sharpening their attacks on President Donald Trump over the economic fallout from the Iran war as rising fuel and household costs become an increasingly potent issue ahead of November’s midterm elections.

A silent letter on state TV turned Iran's top diplomat into an enemy of the faith. One extra letter on Iranian state TV turned Abbas Araghchi into the minister of the Kharijites, the sect that abandoned Shia Islam's first imam and killed him, prompting some Iranians to read it as the broadcaster's latest shot at the man negotiating with Washington.

Tehran weighs benefits of brief Hormuz reprieve. With a deadline to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz only days away, parts of Iran’s media are increasingly treating any easing of tensions not as a return to normality but as a brief window to replenish essential supplies before the confrontation potentially resumes.

Iran’s security reshuffle lays bare political drama at the top. The ascension of Mohsen Rezaei as secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council underscores that there is much political drama beneath the surface of the Islamic Republic’s portrayal of strength as the Trump administration tries to end the war.

Fear of unrest complicates Iran’s gasoline dilemma. The aborted move in Kerman Province revived one of the most politically explosive questions in Iran: how to curb gasoline consumption without repeating the upheaval that followed the last major nationwide price increase in 2019.

Iran hits back after Trump says he may declare Hormuz US territory. President Donald Trump said he may soon declare the Strait of Hormuz US territory as shipping through the waterway nearly stopped and Tehran insisted it alone would decide when the strait opens or closes.

Sanctions alone cannot topple Iran’s regime, former Treasury official says. Sanctions can make Iran’s military and nuclear activities costlier and more difficult but cannot bring down the Islamic Republic on their own, former US Treasury official and weapons procurement expert Kerri Bitsoff told Iran International.

War redraws Iran’s trade as ties with key partners plunge. Iran says its non-oil trade has fallen by around 30% since the war began, but figures from several of its biggest trading partners point to far steeper declines in some of the country’s most important commercial relationships.

Iran’s rulers turn attention to the threat from within. As Iran confronts military pressure abroad and mounting economic strain at home, signs are emerging that the Islamic Republic is increasingly turning its attention to another potential threat: renewed unrest on its own streets.

Qatar rejects Iran's claim it captured three Su-24 pilots alive. Qatar on Saturday dismissed the Iranian military’s claim that it had detained and held three pilots from two Su-24 bombers shot down in March, saying it recovered only one pilot’s remains and had invited Tehran to review the search.

Mohsen Rezaei’s son among nine identified in $11-billion Iran oil network. Relatives of some of Iran’s most powerful security figures, including Mohsen Rezaei’s son, were among nine people tied to an oil-sales network that sources say failed to return about $11 billion in proceeds, an Iran International investigation found.

Iran executes man accused of driving into police during January protests. Iran executed Shahram Sadeghi early Sunday after accusing him of security offenses and deliberately driving into police officers during protests in Karaj on January 8, the judiciary’s Mizan News reported.

Iran lawmaker played direct role in deadly protest crackdown, witnesses say. Jafar Pourkabgani, a lawmaker representing the southern Iranian province of Bushehr and a former longtime member of the IRGC and Basij, personally fired at protesters during nationwide demonstrations in January, witnesses told Iran International.

Iran weighs gasoline rationing as fuel deficit widens. Iran’s government is considering three proposals to curb gasoline consumption as war damage, import difficulties and a widening gap between domestic production and demand put growing pressure on fuel supplies.

The three snakes of Zahhak. In the Persian classic Shahnameh, Ferdowsi tells the story of Zahhak, the usurper king who is kissed on each shoulder by Ahriman, the spirit of evil, and finds two black snakes growing from the wounds.

Iraqi Kurdistan president’s office confirms Barzani’s US-Iran backchannel role. Iraqi Kurdistan President Nechirvan Barzani played a role in relaying messages between the United States and Iran and in efforts to ease tensions, a spokesperson confirmed to Iran International on Sunday.

Iran’s new infiltration bill could make ordinary contact a crime. Iranian lawmakers have advanced sweeping legislation that could send people to prison for speaking to journalists, academic cooperation and unauthorized contact with foreign embassies, dramatically expanding the conduct security agencies could treat as foreign infiltration.

« Africa Corps Airline » : comment la Russie achemine armes et troupes au Sahel. Un rapport de l’ONG américaine C4ADS lève le voile sur la logistique aérienne d’Africa Corps. Sept compagnies, dont des opérateurs publics russes et africains, alimentent les bases au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Niger.

Maroc : les promoteurs immobiliers en plein âge d’or ?. Addoha, Alliances, Résidences Dar Saada : l’immobilier marocain renoue avec la croissance. Portés par la Coupe du monde 2030 et l’aide directe au logement, les grands promoteurs du royaume affichent des bilans assainis et des carnets de commandes bien garnis.

Cameroun : comment la Sosucam a changé de mains. Alors que Somdia, filiale du groupe Castel, avait annoncé son retrait de la première sucrerie du Cameroun, un consortium local, comptant l’avocat Joseph Pagop Noupoué mais aussi Henriette Noutchougouin et William Nkontchou, reprend le flambeau.

« Oui, je le veux ! » : en RDC, Grâce Kutino, porte-voix d’un changement de Constitution. La ministre de la Jeunesse et de l’Éveil patriotique était à la tête de milliers de manifestants qui se disent favorables à l’adoption d’une Loi fondamentale qui réponde à leurs aspirations.

Le Cameroun peut-il redevenir une fédération ?. Le 14 août 1961, la Constitution fédérale du Cameroun était adoptée à Yaoundé. Depuis, la fédération a disparu et Paul Biya, au pouvoir depuis 1982, a toujours été le défenseur d’un État unitaire. Mais le débat sur le fédéralisme reste d’actualité.

Tchad : ce que l’on sait du conflit entre l’Autorité de lutte contre la corruption et l’Agence de sécurité de l’État. Des agents de l’ANSE ont interpellé plusieurs contrôleurs de l’AILC qui enquêtaient sur la gestion de la Société des hydrocarbures du Tchad. L’institution anticorruption soupçonne que l’intervention soit liée à une autre affaire, impliquant le frère du patron des renseignements.

Qui est Emaar, le groupe émirati qui signe son retour au Maroc ?. Spécialiste des mégaprojets immobiliers, Emaar, fondé par Mohamed Alabbar, pourrait construire un nouveau complexe dans la région de Casablanca. Ce projet remet en lumière les ambitions africaines du géant émirati.

Tchad : Succès Masra gracié par Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, l’espoir d’une « nouvelle page » pour l’opposant. Le président tchadien a accordé ce 14 août une grâce à neuf personnalités, dont l’opposant Succès Masra. Pour ce dernier, de nouvelles tractations commencent, avec comme objectif un nouveau retour au premier plan de la politique tchadienne.

Niger-Algérie : Sonatrach marque un point dans la réalisation de ses ambitions pétrolières. La compagnie pétrolière algérienne Sonatrach vient de lancer les opérations de forage d’un puit à Kafra, dans le nord du Niger. Une façon pour les deux pays d’acter leur rapprochement après des mois de tensions diplomatiques.

Dîna Slaoui, la Marocaine qui a ouvert les portes du monde très fermé des diamantaires. Première Marocaine à intégrer la Bourse du diamant d’Anvers, Dîna Slaoui s’est frayé un chemin dans un univers où réputation et confiance font loi. De Casablanca aux coulisses du négoce mondial, portrait d’une passionnée qui connaît les diamants sous toutes leurs facettes.

Mustafa Rawji (Rawbank) : « Notre priorité, c’est désormais l’économie réelle, celle qui crée de l’emploi ». Face aux défis de la RDC et à l’émergence de la concurrence, Rawbank adapte son modèle. Son dirigeant veut conforter la position de leader régional de la banque, en axant sur les PME et les investisseurs internationaux attirés par les grands projets régionaux.

Barrick : pourquoi l’Afrique reste au cœur de la stratégie internationale du géant minier. En séparant ses actifs nord-américains du reste, Barrick redessine son portefeuille mondial. À la tête du « Rest of the world », Sebastiaan Bock hérite d’un ensemble où l’Afrique pourrait peser lourd.

Au Sénégal, le patrimoine de Bassirou Diomaye Faye au cœur d’un nouveau bras de fer avec Ousmane Sonko. Le Pastef veut contraindre Bassirou Diomaye Faye à déclarer son patrimoine en fin de mandat. Le chef de l’État contre-attaque en visant aussi Ousmane Sonko. Analyse d’un nouvel épisode de la guerre à laquelle se livrent les deux hommes.

Quand les élèves d’Azrou se retournent contre le Protectorat. La « politique berbère » du Protectorat reposait sur le maintien des élèves du collège d’Azrou à distance des courants qui agitaient le reste du Maroc. Pourtant, au début des années 1940, les certitudes de « la Résidence » se lézardent. Au cœur même de son dispositif scolaire émerge une conscience politique qu’elle n’a su ni anticiper ni contenir.

RDC : la loi sur le référendum renvoyée devant le Parlement, Félix Tshisekedi maître des horloges. Le président, Félix Tshisekedi, a renvoyé au Parlement la loi référendaire en demandant la modification de certains de ses articles. Un report qui intervient au moment où l’opposition appelle à l’apaisement avant l’ouverture d’un potentiel dialogue national.

La Cour africaine des droits de l’homme est-elle encore utile ?. Créée pour protéger les droits fondamentaux sur le continent, la Cour africaine des droits de l’homme et des peuples (CADHP) peine à faire appliquer ses décisions : sur les 104 arrêts rendus, seuls deux ont été pleinement exécutés. Décryptage en vidéo.

Comment l’Afrique du Sud a doublé l’Espagne sur l’exportation d’agrumes. En quarante ans, l’Afrique du Sud est passée des boycotts anti-apartheid au sommet du commerce mondial des agrumes. Mais protectionnisme européen, logistique défaillante et El Niño menacent ce succès.

Guinée : Bella Bah, un « activiste dans l’âme » qui dérange Mamadi Doumbouya. L’ancien membre du Front national de défense de la Constitution (FNDC) a été enlevé dans l’école dont il est le directeur, samedi 8 août. Il a finalement été déféré devant un juge, jeudi, et devrait être jugé. Un soulagement pour ses proches, qui craignaient de ne plus jamais le revoir.

Côte d’Ivoire : qui est Martial Yavo, le nouveau général de Charles Blé Goudé ?. Propulsé secrétaire général du Cojep après le départ surprise de Patrice Saraka, cet inspecteur d’éducation, homme de l’ombre et fidèle de la première heure, doit remettre le parti en ordre de bataille. Portrait.

Otage américain au Niger : comment l’administration Trump a obtenu la libération. Enlevé à Niamey en octobre 2024, le missionnaire américain Kevin Rideout a été libéré aprés dix mois de captivité. Une coopération discrète entre Washington et les pays de l’Alliance des États du Sahel a permis son retour.

Succès Masra gracié, Assimi Goïta et Abdelmadjid Tebboune se réconcilient, la crise d’Ormuz profite aux majors… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer. Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique revient sur la grâce accordée à l’opposant tchadien Succès Masra, décrypte la réconciliation entre le Mali et l’Algérie, analyse les bénéfices tirés par les majors de la crise d’Ormuz et le regain d’attractivité des hydrocarbures africains, s’interroge sur un possible report des élections locales au Sénégal et fait le point sur les dernières tractations autour du dialogue national en RDC.

« Le pétrole est une malédiction » : en Ouganda, des villages dans l’incertitude sur la propriété de leurs terres. En Ouganda, la ruée vers l’or noir a exacerbé des conflits fonciers vieux de quinze ans. TotalEnergies et Kampala s’y retrouvent face aux communautés spoliées. Reportage.

Les anciens d’Azrou au sommet de l’État marocain. À la fin du Protectorat, en 1956, le royaume reprend en main l’appareil d’un État devenu indépendant, au sein duquel les anciens élèves d’Azrou vont occuper une place importante, dans toutes les sphères du pouvoir. Des rangs de l’armée aux coulisses du palais en passant par les bureaux de l’administration, ils sont incontournables.

« Nous avons besoin de pardon, d’unité et de paix » : après avoir été libéré, l’opposant tchadien Succès Masra prône la réconciliation. Succès Masra, ancien Premier ministre et chef du principal parti d’opposition au Tchad, fraîchement libéré, a appelé ce 15 août à la réconciliation avec le président Mahamat Idriss Déby devant plusieurs centaines de militants réunis au siège de son parti.

Militaires, technocrates et hommes d’affaires : sur qui Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé s’appuie-t-il pour gouverner le Togo ?. Le président du Conseil, qui concentre l’essentiel des leviers de l’exécutif malgré l’instauration d’une Ve République supposée donner naissance à un régime parlementaire, s’appuie sur un réseau dense au service d’un pouvoir très centralisé.

Uhuru Kenyatta peut-il unifier l’opposition kényane avant qu’il ne soit trop tard ?. Quatre ans après avoir quitté State House, Uhuru Kenyatta tente de monter une coalition capable de battre William Ruto en 2027. Les chefs de l’opposition parviendront-ils à mettre leurs ambitions personnelles de côté ?

Attentat de Skhirat, « coup d’État des aviateurs »… La malédiction d’Azrou. L’ascension des anciens d’Azrou au sein des institutions du royaume les a conduits au plus près du trône. Lorsque cet équilibre vole en éclats, au début des années 1970, le collège hérite d’une réputation sulfureuse, qui occultera pendant des décennies certains acteurs et épisodes d’une histoire bien plus complexe, celle du Maroc moderne.

Guinée : entre exil, prison et participation, l’opposition à Mamadi Doumbouya sous pression. Avec la mise hors-jeu des partis historiques et de leurs leaders contraints à l’exil – parmi lesquels Cellou Dalein Diallo, Sidya Touré et Alpha Condé –, l’opposition guinéenne se recompose comme elle peut dans un espace politique dominé par la formation présidentielle et ses alliés.

Auchan, Carrefour, Marjane… Comment les supermarchés relèvent le défi du local dans les rayons. La grande distribution se pose en fer de lance de l’essor du « Made in Africa » sur le continent. Si les résultats sont réels sur les produits frais et sur la structuration des filières agricoles, il reste encore beaucoup à faire pour généraliser le mouvement.

Starlink : pourquoi la généralisation de l’accès à internet par satellite inquiète les États africains. Au cours des cinq dernières années, le réseau satellitaire de SpaceX aura réussi à obtenir des autorisations de déploiement dans 29 pays du continent. Cet essor fulgurant renforce l’inclusion numérique des populations, tout en mettant en péril la souveraineté des États signataires. Le jeu en vaut-il la chandelle ?

En Libye, le retour diplomatique des Américains, après quinze ans d’effacement. Le conseiller spécial de Donald Trump pour les affaires arabes et africaines, Massad Boulos, cherche un accord entre les familles Haftar et Dbeibah, qui se partagent le pays.

Le Sénégal et la Gambie redéfinissent leurs frontières communes, héritées de la colonisation. Le 29 juillet, un accord définitif a été finalisé pour clarifier le tracé des 749 kilomètres de frontière terrestre entre les deux pays, a annoncé le Secrétariat permanent sénégalo-gambien. Cette frontière avait été dessinée « sur une carte à main levée dans un huis clos parisien », le 10 août 1889.

Yann Vézilier, l’agent de la DGSE condamné au Mali à vingt ans de prison, a été gracié. Après un an de détention, Yann Vézilier, qui était dûment accrédité comme officier de la direction générale de la sécurité extérieure auprès des autorités maliennes, a été gracié jeudi par le chef de la junte, le général Assimi Goïta. Une libération obtenue au terme de plusieurs mois de tractations diplomatiques.

Soudan : Khartoum visée par des frappes de drones des paramilitaires pour le deuxième jour de suite. Les paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide ont lancé mercredi une vaste attaque coordonnée de drones, visant la capitale et d’autres villes contrôlées par l’armée, distantes de plusieurs centaines de kilomètres.

Ebola en RDC : l’épidémie s’étend à une sixième province et menace le Soudan du Sud. Une personne est morte de la maladie dans la province du Bas-Uele (nord), frontalière de la République centrafricaine et jusqu’à présent épargnée.

Pour lutter contre Ebola, la réponse internationale prise de vitesse. Depuis l’épidémie ouest-africaine de 2014-2016 et celle de Covid-19 en 2020, la « préparation aux pandémies » est devenue un mot d’ordre international. Cela n’a pas empêché de nouvelles failles d’apparaître à l’occasion de cette nouvelle crise. L’argent, même lorsqu’il est disponible, arrive souvent trop tard.

Le missionnaire américain, Kevin Rideout, enlevé au Niger en octobre, a été « libéré », selon le groupe chrétien SIM International. Kevin Rideout travaillait comme missionnaire au Niger depuis dix-neuf ans, notamment comme pilote pour le groupe chrétien, selon le « New York Times ».

Elections présidentielle et parlementaires en Zambie : le dépouillement suspendu en raison de « violences », annonce la Commission électorale. Peu avant l’annonce, Brian Mundubile, principal opposant au président sortant Hakainde Hichilema, a revendiqué la victoire dès le premier tour, tandis que M. Hichilema a réagi en appelant les Zambiens à rester « patients ».

Le Quai d’Orsay exprime sa « très grande satisfaction » après la libération de l’agent français Yann Vézilier condamné au Mali. Accusé de conspiration contre les institutions maliennes, l’agent de renseignement français avait été arrêté en août 2025 puis condamné à vingt ans de prison en juin pour « atteinte à la sûreté de l’Etat ».

« On est en train de perdre notre jeunesse » : dans le nord du Maroc, l’ombre des noyés de Ceuta. A Tétouan, les familles se désespèrent après la mort de nombreux hommes qui ont tenté le passage à la nage jusqu’à l’enclave espagnole, fin juillet. Au total, plus de 140 d’entre eux auraient perdu la vie, selon une ONG marocaine. Malgré ces drames, beaucoup rêvent encore de gagner clandestinement l’Europe.

Au Soudan du Sud, plus de 650 000 réfugiés menacés de perdre l’aide de l’ONU. Cette situation « survient au pire moment possible. Avec la saison des pluies qui atteint son pic, l’accès devient plus difficile, les prix de la nourriture augmentent et les familles disposent d’encore moins de solutions pour faire face à la situation », a alerté le représentant adjoint du HCR au Soudan du Sud.

Au Soudan, une attaque des paramilitaires des FSR fait au moins 14 morts parmi les civils au Kordofan du Nord. Des dizaines d’autres personnes ont été blessées lors de cet assaut mené par les rebelles à Umm Arda, à environ 200 kilomètres au sud de la capitale, Khartoum. Plusieurs villes soudanaises sont le théâtre d’attaques de plus en plus intenses menées par les FSR.

Au Tchad, neuf opposants, dont Succès Masra, libérés après avoir été graciés par le président, Mahamat Idriss Déby. Ancien premier ministre et chef du principal parti d’opposition, Succès Masra purgeait depuis plus d’un an une peine de vingt ans de prison ferme. Les huit autres dirigeants de parti étaient condamnés pour avoir fomenté une insurrection.

Cartographie : le durcissement de la politique migratoire de Donald Trump en Afrique. A partir du 20 août, le montant de la caution exigée des demandeurs de visa originaires de 50 pays, dont 30 en Afrique, sera augmenté.

Au Kenya, la mort préoccupante d’éléphants, victimes de mystérieux empoisonnements. Au moins 16 pachydermes sont morts dans des circonstances inexpliquées depuis le mois de juin dans la région d’Amboseli, dans le sud du Kenya. L’hypothèse d’une intoxication due à des pesticides est remise en cause par plusieurs experts.

Zimbabwe : le bilan du naufrage d’un ferry sur le lac Kariba s’élève à 68 morts. Les secours ont repêché 22 nouveaux corps, a annoncé la police, samedi. Celle-ci n’a fourni aucun détail sur ces nouvelles victimes, mais la plupart des passagers du navire étaient des villageois et des marchands de poisson vivant aux abords du lac.

Pourquoi le transfert de milliers de tonnes d’uranium congolais vers la Chine pose question ? Comprendre en trois minutes. En vingt ans, environ 2 000 tonnes d’uranium auraient quitté clandestinement la République démocratique du Congo, principalement à destination de la Chine.

En Sierra Leone, la cohabitation exemplaire des chrétiens et des musulmans, loin des tensions confessionnelles des pays de la région. Contrairement au Mali, au Niger, au Burkina Faso ou au Nigeria, minés par les divisions religieuses, l’ancienne colonie britannique voit sa population vivre sereinement sa foi. Chaque famille ou presque est interconfessionnelle, et les leaders religieux n’ont de cesse de promouvoir la cohésion nationale.

Coupe d’Afrique des nations féminine : le Malawi à une victoire de l’un des plus beaux exploits du tournoi. Les Scorchers, emmenées par les sœurs Temwa et Tabitha Chawinga, ont déjoué tous les pronostics en se qualifiant pour la finale, qu’elles disputent contre le Cameroun, dimanche à Rabat. L’équipe, 153ᵉ au classement mondial, n’avait jusqu’alors jamais pris part à la compétition.

« The Polygamist » sur Netflix, la série sud-africaine à succès qui torpille le patriarcat. L’histoire des vies parallèles d’un magnat de l’immobilier narcissique est devenue l’une des dix séries non anglophones les plus regardées sur la plateforme américaine.

Dongfeng’s Voyah Passion S completes tunnel loop stunt for commercial. Voyah, the premium brand of the Dongfeng group, has recreated a vehicle stunt from a commercial nearly two decades ago with their latest electric vehicle. The Voyah Passion S electric SUV drove a loop inside a tunnel, in what Dongfeng claims was a real stunt using a stock car, with no modifications. Only ramps were placed within the tunnel to allow it to form a loop for the car to drive on. The inspiration The stunt is a tribute to one attempted by Mercedes-Benz in 2010. Back then, Mercedes-Benz showed their new SLS AMG sports car driving a loop inside of a tunnel. The stunt was attempted to prove that the vehicle is fast enough to drive upside down for a brief moment, aided by the centrifugal force of the tunnel to allow the vehicle to continue to drive even when upside down. The video featured Michael Schumacher and was shot to announce his return to Formula 1, this time under the Mercedes-Benz F1 team. Despite the incredible feat, the commercial was revealed to be the product of editing trickery, with the car not actually completing the loop, and even more egregiously, was not driven by Michael Schumacher. The new attempt This more recent attempt was performed by Voyah, a premium vehicle brand under the Dongfeng Group, as part of its promotions for its latest upcoming model, the Passion S electric SUV. According to its Weibo page, Dongfeng has gladly acknowledged that it was inspired by the original Mercedes-Benz ad. Unlike its inspiration, the company claims the stunt was performed for real. The automaker chose a closed test tunnel in Wuhan as the venue. The vehicle was a stock Voyah Passion S EV. Its engineers calculated that the car had to hit the first ramp in the tunnel with a steering angle of exactly 16-degrees while traveling at roughly 130 kilometers per hour. This figure would guarantee that the centrifugal force would keep the car’s wheels on the tunnel’s surface (even when upside down). Dongfeng later released a longer one-take video, as part of its efforts to prove that the stunt was indeed performed for real. The longer video shows engineers simulating the stunt in the computer, with a toy car, and eventually preparing the actual tunnel for the stunt, along with a veritable army of firemen, firetrucks, and medical emergency vehicles. The Voyah Passion S The commercial itself was all part of the automaker’s plans to launch the new Passion S. The vehicle is powered by an 800-volt, 98-kilowatt-hour battery pack that enables a CLTC-rated range of 740-km for the two-wheel-drive version, and up to 630-km for the dual-motor all-wheel drive version. The latter delivers 637 horsepower and can spring from 0-100-km/h in 4.5 seconds. It rides on sports car-like double-wishbone in front and a five-link all-aluminum independent suspension at the rear, with electronically controlled dampers and air springs. It also boasts of a quad-lidar advanced driver assistance system that makes use of 33 sensors. Inside, there’s a pair of 15.6-inch displays and a 29-inch augmented reality heads-up display. It is also 5C charging compatible, capable of recharging from 20% to 80% in ten minutes. For now, the Voyah Passion S is only available in China.

Abante: Impeachment trial has hurt VP Duterte's popularity. The perceived popularity of presidential aspirant Vice President Sara Duterte has taken a hit because of her ongoing Senate impeachment trial. Impeachment complaint endorser Manila 6th district Rep. Bienvenido “Benny” Abante Jr. gave this take over the weekend even as the trial continues to showcase evidence against Duterte through the prosecution. “Palagay ko nabawasan na ang rating ng ating Vice President dito (I think the Vice President’s rating has declined because of this,” Abante said. The veteran congressman made these remarks as recent surveys showed strong public interest in having Duterte face the impeachment charges and in seeing the case decided on the evidence. Duterte announced her intention to run for president in the 2028 elections last February, just as multiple impeachment complaints were piling on her at the House of Representatives. But all her popularity and influence would be for naught if she gets convicted by the senator-judges, since she would get penalized with perpetual disqualification from holding public office, on top of removal from her post. “Naniniwala ako na the (I believe that) Vice President is not as popular as before...Nakikita na ng taumbayan ang nangyayari (The people have seen what is happening). And I think that they are deciding, they are actually looking now for evidence,” Abante said. An OCTA Research survey released this month found 55 percent of Filipinos preferred that all evidence be presented before senator-judges decide whether to convict or acquit Duterte. An earlier OCTA survey found 71 percent believed the Senate impeachment court should base its decision on the law and evidence, while a Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey found 70 percent believed Duterte must address the impeachment charges to clear questions surrounding her accountability. According to Abante, this makes the presentation and evaluation of evidence all the more crucial. 'Political cataract' As such, he warned the senator-judges against allowing politics to cloud their judgment. “Sa akin, sinasabi ko, sana hindi maging exercise of politics ito. Dapat ito, makita na ng taong-bayan, makita ng impeachment court mismo itong ebidensya)." (I’m saying, I hope this does not become an exercise of politics. This should be seen by the people, seen by the impeachment court itself as evidence.) “Huwag sanang magkaroon ng blinders o ng tinatawag nating political cataract ang mga senator-judges tungkol diyan,” he added. (I hope there will be no blinders or what we call political cataract among the senator-judges regarding that.) Abante said the impeachment trial has boiled down to searching for the truth rather than protecting political personalities or allegiances. “Ako eh, hindi ko tinatanong kung DDS ka o hindi ka DDS,” Abante referring to "Duterte Diehard Supporters". “Pero kinakailangan makita natin, makita ng taumbayan ang katotohanan.” (As for me, I don’t ask if you’re DDS or not DDS...But it is necessary that we see, that the people see the truth.) “This is no longer [about] personality eh. Katotohanan na ito eh (This is already about the truth),” he noted.

Farm damage from Luis, Maymay, ‘habagat’ tops ₱1 billion. Agricultural damage from tropical cyclones Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon or “habagat” has exceeded ₱1 billion, based on the latest estimate of the Department of Agriculture (DA). In a bulletin on Monday, Aug. 17, the DA said the agriculture sector has incurred ₱1.03 billion in losses from the impact of weather disturbances over the past two weeks. An estimated 25,662 hectares (ha) of agricultural areas have been damaged across the regions of Cordillera, Ilocos, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, and Western Visayas. This has affected a total of 30,073 farmers, with production losses estimated at around 25,280 metric tons (MT). Affected commodities include rice, corn, cassava, high-value crops, fisheries, livestock, and poultry, as well as agri-fisheries infrastructure, machinery, and equipment. The rice sector accounted for more than half of the total losses, with damage estimated at ₱589.44 million, equivalent to a production loss of 16,105 MT. Damage to high-value crops, which include bananas, root crops, papaya, and upland and lowland vegetables, reached 7,772 MT, with a value of ₱313.07 million. “Further damage and losses are expected in affected regions as assessment and validation are ongoing,” the DA said. The DA said it has prepared ₱177.67 million worth of agricultural inputs such as rice, corn, and vegetable seeds to help farmers recover, alongside 1,007 bags of rice from state-run National Food Authority (NFA). Meanwhile, state-run Philippine Crop Insurance Corp. (PCIC) has allocated ₱35.67 million in indemnification for 5,005 affected insured farmers and fisherfolk. The DA said farmers may also tap the Agricultural Credit Policy Council’s (ACPC) survival and recovery loan program to secure zero-interest loans of up to ₱25,000. Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel said providing immediate government assistance is necessary to prevent temporary losses from becoming long-term livelihood setbacks. “We need to respond immediately to the needs of our farmers and fisherfolk after every calamity so they can recover quickly and sustain their livelihoods,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement.

FPH rejects KKR’s ₱35-per-share First Gen offer, says price falls short of true value. The Lopez Group’s First Philippine Holdings Corp. (FPH) has rejected a proposal from Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. L.P. (KKR) to acquire a portion of its stake in First Gen Corp. because the price offered is not good enough. “After careful deliberation and consideration, FPH has determined that KKR’s proposal does not represent First Gen’s true value,” FPH said in a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Monday, Aug. 17. FPH said it has sent a letter advising KKR that it has decided not to pursue KKR’s non-binding proposal to acquire a portion of FPH’s shareholding in First Gen and launch a voluntary tender offer for First Gen’s public float at ₱35 per share. KKR proposed to acquire an additional 20-percent stake in First Gen by initially acquiring an additional 8.43-percent stake in First Gen from parent firm FPH at ₱35 per share for a total amount of ₱10.6 billion. The transaction was to be followed by a tender offer at the same price of ₱35 a share for First Gen’s remaining 11.67-percent public float, with the intention of voluntarily delisting First Gen from the PSE. “Given the significant increase in First Gen’s share price (up 44 percent) since the news came out of KKR’s offer, the decision by FPH to reject the proposal could result [in] a significant correction in First Gen’s share price in the near term,” said COL Financial Group Inc. senior research manager George Ching. He added, “It remains to be seen whether this decision by FPH could pave way for a better offer by KKR or another potential bidder which FPH would consider.” Given First Gen’s limited float of 11.67 percent, Ching said it is very likely that First Gen will be voluntarily delisted in the exercise if more than 1.7 percent of the minority shares accept KKR’s tender offer. “In terms of the ₱35-per-share tender offer price, we believe this is close to First Gen’s fair valuation at this point (COL fair value estimate is ₱34.70 per share). Furthermore, the offer is a significant 64-percent premium to First Gen’s market price,” Ching said last Aug. 12, when KKR had just made the proposal. Chinabank Capital Corp. managing director Juan Paolo Colet said, “By turning down the offer, First Gen keeps the door open for a potentially more attractive proposal, either from KKR or a competing bidder.” “The downside risk for public shareholders is that if no higher offer emerges, the stock price could surrender much of its recent speculation-driven rally. In the absence of a new bid, First Gen should clearly communicate how it plans to unlock shareholder value,” Colet added.

Morocco looks outward. Twenty-seven years on the throne can change a country. For Morocco, the reign of King Mohammed VI has coincided with an ambitious period of modernization that has reshaped its infrastructure, economy and international outlook, while strengthening the Kingdom’s position as a bridge between Africa, Europe and an increasingly wider circle of partners. That transformation provided much of the context when Morocco marked the 27th anniversary of the King’s enthronement in Manila on July 30. Held at Dusit Thani Manila, the reception brought together members of the diplomatic corps, Philippine government officials, business leaders and friends of Morocco for Throne Day, one of the most important occasions on the Moroccan calendar. There was also a bit of humor from Moroccan Ambassador Mohammed Rida El Fassi, who opened his remarks by recalling that he had confidently told guests at last year’s celebration that it would be his final Enthronement Day in the Philippines. “What I thought was a farewell speech should have been a ‘See you next year’ speech,” he joked. A year later, he was back at the podium—and with considerably more to talk about. “Throne Day is a moment of national pride for all Moroccans,” El Fassi said. “It offers an opportunity to reflect on the remarkable transformation of Morocco under the leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI.” Over the past 27 years, he noted, the Kingdom has pursued political, economic and social reforms aimed at promoting inclusive development, strengthening democratic institutions, advancing human rights and improving living conditions. Perhaps the most visible side of that transformation has been Morocco’s modernization drive. Investments in infrastructure, renewable energy, industry and social development have helped position the country as a strategic hub connecting Africa with Europe and the wider world. Geography certainly helps: Morocco sits at the northwestern edge of Africa, just across the Strait of Gibraltar from Europe. But its ambitions increasingly stretch farther into the African continent. El Fassi pointed to the Nigeria-Morocco African Atlantic Gas Pipeline as an example. The initiative envisions connecting Nigeria with Morocco along the Atlantic coast of West Africa, with the broader ambition of strengthening energy security and regional economic integration. For the ambassador, it reflects Morocco’s larger approach to development: using its own growth to create stronger connections across the continent. That outward-looking approach also defines Moroccan diplomacy. Under King Mohammed VI, El Fassi said, Morocco has remained committed to “peace, stability, sustainable development and effective multilateralism,” while pursuing South-South cooperation and expanding partnerships across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Pacific. The Philippines increasingly fits into that picture. Manila and Rabat celebrated 50 years of diplomatic relations in 2025. What began as a relationship separated by considerable geography has gradually expanded into cooperation in trade, tourism, renewable energy, education and culture. The two countries also work together in multilateral institutions, including on issues affecting middle-income countries—an area where nations separated by continents can nevertheless find themselves confronting remarkably similar development challenges. Morocco’s location and connectivity offer Filipino businesses a potential gateway into African and European markets, while the Philippines gives Moroccan companies access to one of Southeast Asia’s largest consumer markets and a country positioned at the center of an increasingly consequential region. That makes the presence of Rustan’s and SSI Group Inc. as partners in this year’s celebration particularly fitting. Diplomatic relations ultimately deepen when government engagement is complemented by business, tourism, education and ordinary encounters between people. Morocco has also become increasingly adept at using culture as part of that international introduction. For many Filipinos, the country is immediately recognizable through images of Marrakech, Casablanca, desert landscapes, intricate architecture and Moroccan cuisine. But behind that familiar visual identity is a country making a deliberate effort to present itself as a modern economy, an investment destination and a diplomatic actor with interests extending well beyond its immediate neighborhood. Morocco and the Philippines may sit on opposite sides of continents, but both occupy interesting geographical positions: one looking toward Africa, Europe and the Atlantic, the other at the crossroads of Southeast Asia and the Indo-Pacific. There is opportunity in connecting those worlds. Throne Day is ultimately a celebration of Morocco and the relationship between its monarch and its people. But this year’s reception in Manila also offered a glimpse of how Morocco increasingly sees its place beyond its borders. Twenty-seven years into the reign of King Mohammed VI, the Kingdom is not simply looking at how far it has come. It is looking at where—and with whom—it wants to go next.

Cebu leaders honor Abalos during provincial visit. CEBU CITY — Cabinet Secretary Benjamin “Benhur” Abalos Jr. was recognized by Cebu’s local leaders during his recent visit to the province, as officials hailed his appointment to the Cabinet as well as his continued engagement with local government units (LGUs) The Cebu Provincial Government, under the leadership of Governor Pamela Baricuatro, and the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, led by Vice Governor Glenn Anthony Soco, joined the League of Municipalities of the Philippines (LMP)–Cebu Chapter, mayors from Cebu’s tri-cities, Cebu City, Mandaue City and Lapu-Lapu City, and the Liga ng Mga Barangay - Cebu Province Chapter, in honoring Abalos through formal resolutions and public tributes. The resolutions cited Abalos’ appointment as Cabinet Secretary and his efforts to maintain close coordination with local governments, particularly in addressing concerns raised by communities and local officials. The recognition took place during a thanksgiving lunch hosted by the LMP–Cebu Chapter, bringing together provincial, city and municipal leaders, including Presidential Assistant for the Visayas Philip Lo, Governor Baricuatro, Vice Governor Soco, Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival, members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and mayors from across the province. While recognition from the Liga ng Mga Barangay - Cebu Province Chapter later took place during a special portion of their 3rd Quarter ABC Chapter Presidents Meeting through Barangay Provincial President, Hon. Celestino A. Martinez III. The thanksgiving lunch also marked the appointment of two fellow Cebuanos to key national government positions. Local leaders congratulated Sec. Philip Lo on his appointment as Presidential Assistant for the Visayas and Usec. Atty. Bret Monsanto on his appointment as Undersecretary of the Office of the President - Office of the Cabinet Secretary. In her remarks, Governor Baricuatro described Abalos as a unifying figure among Cebu’s mayors, highlighting his role in fostering cooperation among local leaders despite political differences. Vice Governor Soco, meanwhile, recalled Abalos’ assistance to communities affected by the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck northern Cebu in October 2025. He noted that Abalos personally extended financial assistance worth PHP 1,000,000 to affected Cebuanos using his own funds. Beyond the recognition, the gathering underscored the importance of sustained coordination between national and local governments, particularly in responding to emergencies and advancing programs and services at the community level. For Cebu’s local leaders, Abalos’ visit also served as an opportunity to strengthen ties with the national government and reaffirm a shared commitment to putting local concerns at the center of public service.

Anne Curtis addresses neck lump concerns, urges fans to prioritize checkups. Anne Curtis has addressed concerns about her health after some netizens noticed what appeared to be a lump on her neck in photos and videos circulating online. Moro Gulf tsunami, 50 years later: What Phivolcs says we should know. Fifty years ago today, a magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck Moro Gulf, followed by a tsunami that devastated coastal communities in Sultan Kudarat and other areas around the gulf. The earthquake struck at 12:11 a.m. on Aug. 17, 1976, when many residents were asleep, thus it is also known as the “Midnight Killer.” In Lebak, Sultan Kudarat, tsunami waves reached as high as nine meters, about the height of a three-story building. The tsunami also caused extensive coastal damage in Kalamansig and Palimbang, “severely affecting fishing communities and leaving widespread damage,” Phivolcs said. About 8,000 people died in the disaster. The 1976 event remains the deadliest tsunami in Philippine history. Lessons from the disaster The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) said residents in coastal areas should know the natural signs of a tsunami, particularly when an earthquake occurs near the coast. The agency uses “Shake, Drop, Roar” to describe these signs. “Shake” refers to strong or prolonged ground shaking, “Drop” refers to an unusual rise or fall in sea level, and “Roar” refers to an unusual sound coming from the sea. People who feel a strong earthquake near the coast should move to higher ground or farther inland, especially if they notice unusual changes in the sea, instead of waiting for an official warning. The same areas hit by the 1976 tsunami have faced another reminder of the hazard this year. On June 8, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake off Sarangani prompted Phivolcs to issue a tsunami warning. Tsunami inundation was later recorded in parts of Lebak and Kalamansig, with water reaching about 163 meters inland in Barangay Clara, Kalamansig. The earthquake was generated by the Cotabato Trench, the same source that produced the 1976 Moro Gulf earthquake. 50th anniversary As the country marks the 50th anniversary of the Moro Gulf earthquake and tsunami, Phivolcs and the local governments of Lebak and Sultan Kudarat are holding commemorative and preparedness activities in the area. A commemorative marker will be unveiled on Aug. 17 at the Provincial Capitol Extension in Barangay Tibpuan, Lebak. The marker “pays tribute to the survivors, responders, scientists, government agencies, local communities, international partners, and media organizations” involved in the response to the 1976 earthquake and tsunami, Phivolcs said. The agency will also distribute earthquake and tsunami information materials to teachers and local disaster risk reduction and management officials. On Aug. 18, an exhibit featuring the 1976 earthquake and interactive earthquake and tsunami preparedness activities will open at the Barangay Aurelio F. Freires Sr. Gymnasium. Grade 7 and 8 students from Lebak and Kalamansig will also attend the “Kabataan: Handa ang May Alam” seminar on geologic hazards and preparedness.

Eat your way to better eye health. In this day and age, we take our eyesight for granted. Our unhealthy lifestyle compromises the health of our eyes. In fact, we abuse our eyes by binge-watching shows, doom-scrolling on our gadgets, playing video games for long hours, reading with poor lighting, not getting enough quality sleep, and the list goes on. We also abuse our gift of eyesight by not getting optimum nutrition to keep our eyes healthy. Did you know that being physically inactive or having a sedentary lifestyle can hurt your eyes? We need exercise and regular physical activity to help us manage our weight and body fat, as well as promote proper blood circulation. Being overweight and having poor blood circulation can lead to medical conditions such as hypertension or high blood pressure and high blood glucose or diabetes mellitus. Both medical conditions can cause damage to the eyes known as retinopathy. Therefore, it is important to keep one’s blood pressure and blood glucose at bay. This can be achieved with regular physical activity, adequate sleep, stress management, and a diet that is rich in wholesome, minimally processed plant food sources that are high in dietary fiber, antioxidants, and phytochemicals or plant nutrients; low in refined sugars, trans or unhealthy fats, and sodium. Thus, go easy on table salt and condiments. Eating ultra-processed and convenience foods like fast food and canned or cured meat products is detrimental to eye health. If you have been diagnosed with hypertension and/or diabetes mellitus, these conditions are reversible at an early stage. Aim to make lifestyle changes with the help of a registered nutritionist-dietitian to adopt healthy lifestyle habits and save your sight, including the rest of your body’s organs. Optimum nutrition and proper hydration are major key factors in keeping your vision healthy. The eyes largely rely on water to produce tears, thus keeping the eyes moist and preventing dryness, redness, and itchiness. A well-hydrated pair of eyes is able to flush out irritants and other toxins. Unfortunately, many people do not have the habit of staying hydrated throughout the day. They only remember to drink water when they are already thirsty or, worse, when their throats are already parched. Have you noticed that your eyes feel more tired and dry when you are also thirsty? That is because you are already dehydrated. Make it a habit to drink one to two glasses of water before, during, and after meals. Drink water between meals even when you are not feeling thirsty. It is wise to carry a water bottle when you are going out just to have water readily available. Drink more water during a hot day or when you are exercising or sweating. A good indicator of proper hydration is when your urine output is light-colored. Dark-colored urine is a sign that you are dehydrated and must immediately drink water. Do you want your vision to be clear? Imagine a world without colors. Healthy vision needs a colorful plate. It simply means that you must consume a variety of fruits and vegetables to get the phytochemicals or plant nutrients that are beneficial to your eyes. Ocular or eye diseases such as diabetic and hypertensive retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, cataracts, and glaucoma are closely related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and dysfunction of the mitochondria, which is the powerhouse of cells in the body. These ocular diseases are major causes of blindness and other visual impairments worldwide. A narrative review conducted by Sandun De Silva and Baojun Xu, titled “Beneficial Effects of Natural Bioactive Compounds on Eye Health,” was published on May 20, 2026. The review critically summarized available evidence on how phytonutrients impact important molecular pathways that are linked with ocular degeneration. These plant chemicals or plant nutrients have antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective (protects nerve cells), and anti-angiogenic (prevents tumor formation) properties. Carotenoids, polyphenols, flavonoids, omega-3 fatty acids, and other bioactive compounds were mentioned in the narrative review. What should we eat more of to save our sight? Carotenoids are yellow, red, and orange pigments found in fruits and vegetables. These can only be obtained from food because the body cannot naturally produce these compounds. Therefore, we must consume yellow, orange, and red-colored fresh produce daily, such as carrots, sweet potatoes, red and yellow bell peppers, tomatoes, squash, papaya, mango, watermelon, cantaloupe, pink guava, red dragon fruit, and more. Did you know that green vegetables also contain carotenoids? Their orange pigment is hidden by the green pigment chlorophyll. Therefore, it is important to eat dark, leafy vegetables such as broccoli, spinach, malunggay, kangkong, and the like. To maximize the absorption of carotenoids, add some healthy fat with omega-3 fatty acids to your carotenoid-rich fruits and vegetables. Omega-3 is found in fatty fish like tuna, salmon, and sardines, but it is also abundant in soy, avocado, oats, psyllium, chia seeds, flaxseeds, kiwi seeds, and walnuts. Polyphenols are found in grapes, berries, dark chocolate, green tea, black tea, red onions, cloves, coffee, turmeric, ginger, black beans, lentils, soy, almonds, chestnuts, pecans, apples, plums, cherries, pears, saffron, and more. Other botanicals contain compounds that also promote eye health. These include ginkgo biloba and ginsenosides found in ginseng. It is best to consult a registered nutritionist-dietitian specializing in integrative and functional nutrition if you wish to add these botanicals to your daily intake. Never neglect your eye health. Save your sight by getting proper nutrition, being physically active, and getting good-quality sleep, in addition to observing other healthy lifestyle habits. Moreover, always visit your eye doctor at least once or twice a year for proper assessment and management. cheshireque@gmail.com

Cherry Pie Picache: Single but hopeful. Cherry Pie Picache is still single following her breakup with Edu Manzano. The two had talked about marriage, although Cherry Pie admitted she had reservations about taking that step, having never been married before. They eventually went their separate ways. Edu has since found new love, while Cherry Pie remains on her own. She is unbothered by it, but admits she remains hopeful that she, too, will find someone to love. “Oo. Kung mangyayari. Kung hindi, e, di hindi,” Cherry Pie said. Asked if she is dating somebody at the moment, she was quick to answer: “Wala pa.” Cherry Pie’s son, Nio, is now 24 and is becoming increasingly independent, leaving the actress to embrace what she describes as her own version of empty-nest life. “He’s busy with work. In his own na, e. Oo. May sarili na siyang schedule. May sarili na siyang activities, di ba? So, it’s getting there.” And so, Cherry Pie is also making room in her life for the possibility of love. “Nagdadasal na ako ng partner,” she said, laughing. Perhaps that is the beauty of being single at this point in life. There is no need to rush, settle or force anything. For Cherry Pie, and for anyone who find themselves on the same boat, there is still so much life to live, and perhaps, somewhere along the way, someone to share it with. Until then, being on your own does not mean being alone.

Classes suspended in Zamboanga City due to high heat index. ZAMBOANGA CITY- Face to face classes were suspended here on Monday, August 17, due to high heat index. Mayor Khymer Olaso suspended classes in all levels in both private and public schools after the heat index was forecast to reach 41 degrees Celsius. High temperatures have been prevailing in Zamboanga for the past two weeks despite the inclement weather experienced in other parts of the country. Meanwhile, Olaso also advised the public to take necessary precautions against heat stroke and other related diseases brought about by the rise in temperature. Work in public and private offices continues despite the class suspension.

4 jail officers foil smuggling of illegal drugs, contrabands inside BJMP facilities. Four jail officers were honored for thwarting the smuggling of illegal drugs from visitors of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) finside several Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP)-supervised facilities. BJMP spokesperson Supt. Jayrex Bustinera saidthe bureau bestowed the honor to Jail Officer 1 (JO1) Mark Lester Saladino, Senior Jail Officer 3 (SJO3) Ariel Morañon, JO1 Queenie Ann Mae Ponpon and JO1 Margel M. Villaro (Caraga) for exercising due diligence and smart disposition, averting the entry of the prohibited items in their respective jails. Saladino was cited for preventing the attempt of a Manila City Jail Female Dormitory male visitor to smuggle 1.080 grams of shabu inside the facility. At the Carigara District Jail in Leyte, Morañon and Ponpon caught a female visitor trying to sneak in tobacco leaves hidden in her undergarment inside the facility. A newly committed PDL at the Butuan City Jail Male Dormitory tried to slip in around .4337 grams of shabu concealed in his waistband but this did not escape the eagle-eyes of Villaro. “Simple lang ang kanilang ginawa, sinunod nila ang tamang pamamaraan, at hindi sila natakot gumawa ng tama kahit walang nakatingin. Iyan ang uri ng kahusayan na gustong makita ng ating pamunuan sa bawat isa sa atin, oras-oras, araw-araw (What they did was very simple, they adhered to standard protocols, showing no fear to do what is right even if no one was looking. That is the attribute that our leadership wants to see in everyone of us, every time, everyday),’’ BJMP chief Director Efren A. Nemeño emphasized. Nemeño pointed out that the series confiscation of illegal drugs and contrabands is a testament to the jail guard’s effective training and preparedness in ensuring the protection of the BJMP’s facilities. Simultaneous with the enhanced security measures, Nemeño lamented that the BJMP has also relentlessly pursued modernized measures in “humane safekeeping.’’ He assured that all PDLs under the care of the BJMP will be treated equally with absolutely no room for special treatment accorded to influential or high-profile inmates. Nemeño warned the public that the full force of the law awaits anyone who tries to bring in illegal drugs and other similar merchandise inside the BJMP facilities. “Ang mga hakbang na ito ay sumasalamin sa tapat na layunin ng ahensya na mapanatili ang kaayusan at mahigpit na seguridad (inside the jail facility), na siya namang susi tungo sa tuluy-tuloy at epektibong rehabilitasyon ng bawat PDL (These initiatives coincide with the agency’s loyal objective to maintain the orderly and strict security, that are key factors in the continuous and effective rehabilitation of every PDL),’’ Nemeño continued.

RM’s Instagram post draws debate among BTS fans. RM’s recent Instagram post has sparked another round of debate among BTS fans, days after he and J-Hope attended a concert featuring Chris Brown and Usher, Aug. 12. Their appearance drew criticism from some members of ARMY because of Brown’s history of violence, while others defended the BTS members’ decision to attend. Brown pleaded guilty in 2009 to assaulting then-girlfriend Rihanna and was sentenced to five years of probation and six months of community labor. He has also faced other violence-related allegations and incidents over the years. The issue resurfaced on Aug. 16, when RM posted an Instagram Story featuring a Black woman holding an “I love RM” sign from a BTS concert. Some fans questioned the timing and choice of the post, particularly amid the ongoing discussion over his attendance at Brown’s concert. One fan wrote on Threads: “RM posting this in his story makes me extremely uncomfortable for reasons I cannot properly put into words, but apart from the continuing refusal to acknowledge that he platformed an abuser, to my gut it feels supremely performative to feature an apparently adoring Black person considering the current discussions.” Other reactions were similarly critical, with some fans saying RM should be more mindful of his influence and the choices he makes publicly. “I understand people’s zeal to live life their way, but when one is celebrity influencing generations, one needs to be responsible for their actions. I do not relate with him anymore and unfollowed him on Instagram. I will not be going to SFMOMA RM too, and no one should be going,” another fan posted. Another reaction questioned whether RM was using the image of a Black fan to deflect criticism: “But look, I have black fans. U forgive me, right?” “He knows he just doesn't give a f—,” another fan wrote.

Hayden Panettiere, ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville’ star, dies at 36. Hayden Panettiere, the actress who rose to fame as a child and became widely known for “Heroes” and “Nashville,” has died at 36. Her representative confirmed her death to ABC News. No cause of death has been disclosed. Her father, Skip Panettiere, remembered his daughter as a remarkable presence whose impact reached far beyond her family and friends. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” he said. The family has asked for privacy as they grieve her loss. Panettiere began working as a child and built a career across television and film. She became a familiar face to audiences through “Heroes,” in which she played cheerleader Claire Bennet, and later starred as country singer Juliette Barnes in “Nashville.” Her other credits included “Remember the Titans,” “I Love You, Beth Cooper,” “Scream 4” and “Scream VI.” Earlier this year, Panettiere also opened up about her life in her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” released in May. The book offered a deeply personal account of her experiences in Hollywood and her struggles away from the spotlight.

Box Office: ‘Spider-Man’ stays on top while two dino movies battle for third. Two very different dinosaur movies took a modest bite out of the North American box office this weekend, although neither came close to challenging “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” for the top spot or “The Odyssey” for second place. “The End of Oak Street,” an original PG-13 action film starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor, narrowly edged out the animated “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” in their opening weekends. According to studio estimates released Sunday, “The End of Oak Street” earned an estimated $21 million from 3,446 theaters in the US and Canada. “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” followed closely with $20.5 million from 3,545 locations. Neither film came close to “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which continued its dominant run in North America. The Sony Pictures release added another $70 million domestically, bringing its US and Canadian total to $785.8 million. That makes it the fourth-highest-grossing domestic release of all time. With another $118.7 million from international markets, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has now crossed the $2 billion mark worldwide. It is only the eighth movie to reach that milestone without adjusting for inflation and the second-fastest to do so. “Avengers: Endgame” reached $2 billion in 11 days in 2019, while “Brand New Day” took about 18 days. “The Odyssey,” meanwhile, remained in second place in its fifth weekend with $23.2 million. Its domestic total has reached $504.7 million. Christopher Nolan’s epic has also performed strongly overseas, where it has earned $98 million. Its global haul now stands at more than $1.2 billion, helped by its $36.6 million opening days in China. “The End of Oak Street” performed better than expected, collecting $21 million domestically and another $26 million internationally for a worldwide opening of $47 million. The film reportedly cost $80 million to produce. Directed and written by David Robert Mitchell, the movie follows suburban parents played by McGregor and Hathaway whose neighborhood is mysteriously transported to prehistoric times. Critics have responded positively, with the film currently holding an 86% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Audiences were somewhat less enthusiastic, giving it a B CinemaScore. “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” meanwhile, drew families to theaters for its opening weekend. The Paramount Pictures release received an A CinemaScore from audiences and has so far earned $69 million worldwide. The Katseye documentary “Katseye: Wild Hearts” rounded out the top five with $4 million from 724 screens. Other new releases in the top 10 included “Six: The Musical Live,” which opened sixth with $3 million, and “The Brink of War,” which earned $2.7 million. The Tamil-language romance “Vishwanath & Sons” landed in 10th place with $1.6 million. Outside the top 10, Matthew McConaughey’s crime thriller “The Rivals of Amziah King” opened with just over $1 million from 632 theaters.
